252.text: "*Almost* doesn't count, honey. Sounds like you've got to try harder."

253.speaker: Player
253.text: "Congratulations, my girl! But you know I'd love you even if you got bad grades, right?"

254.speaker: Narrator
254.text: I heard a mix of pride and disappointment in her voice."

255.speaker: Player
255.text: "Oh my. We've got a genius in the house! Watch out, world, Holsord's number-two student is on the loose!"

260.text: Monica quickly stood up and snatched the paper from my hands.

267.text: "That's great to hear! I wish your brother had your brains."

268.speaker: Deana
268.text: "Mama says Franc's smart in a different way."

270.speaker: Deana
270.text: "I know! But I still feel kinda bad..."

271.speaker: Deana
271.text: "And then there's that stupid blonde boy Markus. He never even studies, but the teachers always give him higher grades than everyone else."

272.speaker: Monica
272.text: "Don't call him stupid, baby. Who is this Markus?"

273.speaker: Deana
273.text: "I told you about him, Mommy. Markus Clavin. The one who can't even do basic math, remember?"

275.speaker: Player
275.text: "Your mother's right, Deana. Forget about it. You've already done great."

276.speaker: Player
276.text: "Oh, really? Maybe I should have a talk with your school."

278.speaker: Deana
278.text: "What do you mean by talk, Papa?"

279.speaker: Deana
279.text: "Please don't come to the school and shout at the teachers like Markus' father did."

282.speaker: Player
282.text: "Anyway, it doesn't matter, Deana. You've already done great. Don't mind that kid."

288.speaker: Deana
288.text: "Ever since they started letting the girls take science classes, they've been distracting us during exams."

291.speaker: Deana
291.text: "I'm sure I would've been at the top if the boys at school weren't so annoying."

292.speaker: Deana
292.text: "I'm sure I would've been at the top if I'd done better in handicrafts."

295.speaker: Deana
295.text: "His father came to the school a couple of times and shouted at the teachers."

297.speaker: Player
297.text: "He did, did he? Looks like I have a *lot* of talking to do."

298.speaker: Player
298.text: "Some people just have bad manners, darling. You shouldn't pay attention to them."

300.speaker: Monica
300.text: "We'll be back in a bit, sweetie."

301.speaker: Narrator
301.text: We entered the kitchen and Monica closed the door behind us.

305.speaker: Monica
305.text: "Anton. I know the Aschraf Anniversary will take place in a few days. I don't want you to attend."

306.speaker: Monica
306.text: "You know it's the largest-ever commemoration of the Izzam Incident. And it will be swarming with Bludish separatists."

307.speaker: Monica
307.text: "Anton. I have a bad feeling about this. Isn't the Aschraf Anniversary in a few days?"

308.speaker: Monica
308.text: "I feel like something might happen on that day. It's the commemoration of the Izzam Incident after all. And it'll be swarming with Bludish separatists."

309.speaker: Monica
309.text: "With everything going on in Bergia, and the timing of the letter... This cannot be a coincidence."

310.speaker: Player
310.text: "Don't worry, Monica. The anniversary won't even take place. All mass gatherings are banned for the remainder of the emergency."

311.speaker: Player
311.text: "No, Monica. I cannot allow fear to dictate my actions. I cannot let the Bludish people down. You have to trust me."

312.speaker: Player
312.text: "That's exactly what they want us to do, Monica. We cannot give in to their threats. Don't worry. I will take the necessary security precautions."

316.speaker: Player
316.text: "Don't worry, Monica. I will not attend the anniversary. I will not take any risks."

317.speaker: Player
317.text: "If I don't show support for the victims of Izzam now, I fear things may turn out even uglier. We can't let that happen."

318.speaker: Monica
318.text: "You cannot simply decide that by yourself. This is about all of us."

320.speaker: Player
320.text: "Look. You have to trust me. If there is a threat, I will handle it."

321.speaker: Player
321.text: "You're underestimating our forces and the power of the state. Nobody will let a bunch of misguided militants threaten us."

322.speaker: Player
322.text: "Please, Monica. You have to understand me. This political mess can only be solved through diplomacy."

324.speaker: Monica
324.text: "Please, Anton. Listen to me this time."

330.speaker: Monica

330.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Turn08_Decree_WomensRights"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.WomensRightCommission"] == false)  or  Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Monica_Divorce"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Monica_Opinion"] < 0

332.text: "No. They were never to be completely trusted. We must be careful."

333.speaker: Player
333.text: "No, Monica. I have great reservations about them after this letter. Don't worry, I will try to get to the root of it."

334.speaker: Player
334.text: "We shouldn't jump to conclusions immediately. They are tasked with protecting our family."

335.speaker: Monica
335.text: "You have to do something about our security."

337.speaker: Player
337.text: "Don't worry. We'll weather this together. I will take the necessary measures."

338.speaker: Player

349.text: "I've also seen that more and more protests have been popping up around the country lately."

350.speaker: Monica
350.text: "I'm worried that things may get out of hand."

351.speaker: Player
351.text: "There's no need for concern. People are just voicing their criticism."

352.speaker: Player
352.text: "I'm aware. It concerns me as well. But I'll take all the necessary steps, don't you worry."

353.text: "Well, there's nothing I can do about that. Can I?"

354.speaker: Player
354.text: "They're just a bunch of traitors who are being supported by foreign powers. The moment they truly pose a threat, they will be taken care of."

356.text: "Listen to yourself. I think you need a break, Anton."

418.speaker: Narrator
418.text: How real was the threat to my family? Did I really have the power to guarantee their safety?

419.speaker: Narrator

421.speaker: Monica
421.text: "I understand. But honestly, maybe it was all for the best in the end."
